questions.prompt: Two runs of reset(seed=7) plus 500 identical steps give a maximum qpos difference of 3e-4 on the same machine. What do you check first?
options: Whether your forward kinematics uses the right link lengths. Wrong lengths would also shift the tool pose in every run.
Whether the physics time step should be made even smaller.
Any randomness that does not come from np.random.default_rng(seed), such as global random state or set ordering.
Whether the URDF mass matches the MJCF mass.
questions.explanation: On one machine a seeded simulation is a function of its seed; a difference means some state outside the seed leaked in.

questions.prompt: 27 successes in 30 episodes. Lower end of the Wilson 95 % interval, precision 0.005.
questions.skillLabel: Success rates and the Wilson bound

questions.prompt: An MJCF has no <compiler> tag and a hinge with range="-90 90". What does this range mean?
options: Plus and minus 90 degrees, because degrees are the MJCF default.
It is invalid without an explicit angle attribute. MuJoCo refuses to compile such a model and reports an error.
questions.explanation: MuJoCo's compiler angle attribute defaults to degree; a URDF limit would be 1.571 rad.

questions.prompt: A joint 0.25 m from the tool has a small angle error. Which error in degrees moves the tool by 1 mm? Precision 0.01.
Which requirement is falsifiable in the sense of the SPEC.md format?
options: The robot should be accurate. It must behave well in every situation the lab will present.
The code should be clean and well structured.
Idle base drift over 5 s is below 2 mm, checked by test_rest_stability.
questions.explanation: It has a metric, a threshold and a named test that can fail.

questions.prompt: MJCF mass 3.18 kg, URDF mass 3.10 kg. Relative difference in percent (divide by the MJCF mass), precision 0.05.
Describe a test that shows the URDF and the MJCF describe the same robot, and say what failure each part of it catches.
rubric: Compares joint names and limits within a tolerance of about 1e-6 (catches missing joints and degree/radian slips).
Compares total mass within about 2 % (catches missing bodies or unit slips).
Compares forward-kinematics tool positions for random configurations within about 1 mm (catches axis sign and offset errors).
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Why does the FK test use 20 random joint configurations rather than only the zero pose?
options: Random configurations make the test run longer, which improves confidence. A longer run also exposes rare numerical issues in the solver.
Axis sign or offset errors can cancel at the zero pose and only show when joints move.
MuJoCo cannot compute forward kinematics at the zero pose.
The zero pose is outside the joint limits.
questions.explanation: Many mistakes are invisible when every angle is zero.
